investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T09:20:50Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents, indicating the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation because the org-scoped remote agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because the eval probe cannot create an agent, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is collected and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet. This is an eval failure reflecting a real API-layer constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" when the eval runner called POST /api/agents (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime). The eval probe in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent() at line 1339 as its first substantive step; because that call fails immediately with a quota conflict, the probe exits before writing any evidence, leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence, failed-check.evidence). The quota limit is enforced by the swarm/agents API layer, not by the eval runner itself. The most likely underlying condition is that a prior eval run (or runs) created remote agents that were not cleaned up, consuming all 100 slots available to the probe org. The withCleanup wrapper visible at run-status-probes.mjs:1337 is intended to delete agents after each run, but if cleanup failed or was skipped in a previous run, leaked agents would accumulate against the quota.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on Agent Runtime Endpoint in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed because the agent runtime returned a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error with HTTP 404, indicating the harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner was unreachable or running an incompatible version at the time of the run. As a direct consequence, the SSE stream never emitted a generation_completed frame and no image URL was produced, causing both required contract assertions to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1438) issued an SSE request to /api/generate/image/stream in the production-api runtime environment. The server-side agent runtime responded with a 404 and error code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED, meaning the harness endpoint the production-api backend depends on to open an image-generation session was not found. This caused the stream to emit generation_error instead of generation_completed, and imageUrlPresent remained false. The root cause is localized to the agent runtime session-open path in the production-api environment; it is not proven to affect the desktop-release variant of the same check (which is registered as required=true and has no reported failure here). No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so this is an eval-layer failure only — a production user impact cannot be confirmed from the supplied data.
